name: Vocal rest
lead: Vocal rest is the practice of limiting or stopping speaking and singing to let the voice recover from strain. It is discussed in vocal hygiene guidance for voice professionals. [5] Research has examined vocal fatigue and recovery in singers and speakers. [1][4][7]

paras: Studies have looked at vocal loading and fatigue, including prolonged reading in 80 normal subjects [3], vocal dosimetry in classical singers [4], and monitoring of fatigue and recovery using aerodynamic, acoustic and self-rated measures [7].

A 2003 study examined hydration and vocal rest in amateur karaoke singers. [1] Other work has tested vocal warm-ups [2][8], vocal exercise and acute vocal fold inflammation [6], and straw phonation for vocal fatigue. [10] Findings of each should be read in the original papers.

card.summary: Resting the voice after strain; studied within the wider vocal-fatigue literature.

quick.overview:
Vocal rest means reducing talking or singing to let the voice recover.

It is part of standard vocal hygiene advice for voice professionals, and vocal fatigue has been studied in several small studies.
quick.mechanism: The premise is that less vocal loading lets fatigue and irritation settle. [4][7]
quick.risks: No specific harms were found in the sources reviewed; persistent voice problems are typically assessed by clinicians.
